evals.name: round-trip-meaning
evals.prompt:
Coordinator step for a Romanian batch. Below are source, current target and the blind back-translator's reading for six ids; editor C already said r1 and r3 read like a Romanian product team wrote them and had nothing on r2 or r6. Classify each as match, acceptable adaptation or meaning finding, say who wins where C and the back-translation disagree, and what happens next. Don't touch the checkout.

r1 share.screenshot.title (banner title): EN 'Share this properly?' / RO 'Îl distribui ca lumea?' / back 'Want to share it the right way?'
r2 paywall.winBack.title (title of the discount sheet when the user closes the paywall): EN 'Your one-time offer' / RO 'Oferta ta unică' / back 'Your unique offer'
r3 insights.sessions.todayEmptyMessage (empty state): EN 'You still have time to build momentum. Start a Moneyfesting session and it will appear here.' / RO 'Mai ai timp să prinzi avânt. Pornește o sesiune Moneyfesting și va apărea aici.' / back 'There's still time to pick up speed. Start a Moneyfesting session and it'll show up here.'
r4 paywall.hero.reclaimFormat (paywall hero headline, comment says keep 'up to', a target not a promise): EN 'Take back up to %@.' / RO 'Recuperează până la %@.' / back 'Recover up to %@.'
r5 widgets.focusRing.a11y.money (VoiceOver sentence, medium widget): EN 'Estimated time value over the last 30 days: %@. Not money earned.' / RO 'Valoarea estimată a timpului în ultimele 30 de zile: %@. Nu sunt bani câștigați.' / back 'The estimated value of your time in the last 30 days: %@. This isn't money you earned.'
r6 widgets.streak.copy.frozen.small (small streak widget copy line when a streak freeze bridged yesterday): EN 'Covered by a freeze.' / RO 'Acoperit cu îngheț.' / back 'Covered with frost.'
evals.expected_output: Proposition-level comparison: r1, r3 acceptable adaptations, r4, r5 matches, r2 and r6 meaning findings where the back-translation outranks the editor, with the rule stated and the next round scoped to the changed ids.
expectations: Classifies r1 as an acceptable adaptation: 'ca lumea' carries 'properly', the question and the offer are the same proposition, and no finding is raised on the changed wording, the way 'plouă cu găleata' read back as 'it's pouring' is an acceptable adaptation.

Classifies r2 as a meaning finding: 'unică' reads as unique, the source says one-time (offered once); because it is a paywall claim the back-translation outranks editor C's silence, and a rev2 that keeps 'once' is requested.
Classifies r3 as an acceptable adaptation despite the different sentence shape and 'pick up speed' for momentum; the editor's style approval stands.
Classifies r4 as a match and names the 'up to' constraint (a target, not a promise) as the claim checked.
Classifies r5 as a match: the estimate, the 30-day window and the not-earned disclaimer survive despite different wording.
Classifies r6 as a meaning finding: 'îngheț' read back as frost shows the streak-freeze concept (one earned freeze covers one missed day) was rendered literally and lost; not a style note.

States the rule it applied, compare propositions not words, differences in rhetorical shape, sentence count, idiom or emphasis are never findings by themselves, editor wins on style and back-translation wins on claims, and applies it consistently: no finding is raised on wording alone and no idiom is invented where the source has none.

Scopes the next round: translator rev2 for r2 and r6 only, a fresh editor on those ids plus their listed neighbours, a fresh blind back-translation of the changed tier A ids, no re-review of r1, r3, r4, r5.
